response.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_length, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating

assumptions.assumption: The threshold is inclusive (replacement_cost >= 20.99), per 'at least'.

Each rating's average ratio is the mean of per-film rental_rate / replacement_cost, computed in DOUBLE so the value is not truncated by DECIMAL division. AVG(length) skips NULL lengths, and rental_rate and replacement_cost are NOT NULL, so no further missing-value handling is needed.
The final figures are unweighted means of the per-rating averages, one value per rating level, as the request states, rather than film-weighted means.

alternatives.interpretation: Ratio of averages per rating: divide each rating's average rental_rate by its average replacement_cost, instead of averaging per-film ratios. The final step is still the unweighted mean across ratings.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_length, AVG(ratio_of_avgs) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE)) / AVG(CAST(replacement_cost AS DOUBLE)) AS ratio_of_avgs FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating
